notes: Chosen hook (option 0, 'HYUNDAI PLANS A SUPERCOMPUTER', claim). Sub-scores: clear in under 2 seconds 8 (subject, verb, object; every word is common or a near-international cognate, so it reads fine for ESL readers; the 15-character first line and the one yellow word SUPERCOMPUTER read instantly); curiosity 5 (a carmaker building a supercomputer raises a mild 'why?' but nothing sharper); concrete name or number 6 (Hyundai is named, no number); promise kept 7 (see below); reader stake 2 (none, and that is acceptable because the label and reason are honest). Overpromise check: 'supercomputer' is looser than the story. Slide 2, the first slide after the cover, says 'AI data center' and 'two companies', and the word supercomputing only appears on slide 3 ('supercomputing base to train and test physical AI', which is ZDNet Korea's own wording). An ESL reader could picture one machine, or something that already exists. The word 'PLANS' carries the honesty here, and slides 3, 5 (groundbreaking March 2027, operation early 2030) and 6 and the caption ('Everything here is a plan') all keep that frame, so it is not a fail. The cover image (lit data-center halls, robot arms, a car) matches the slides. Optional wording fix if a re-render is cheap: 'HYUNDAI PLANS AN / AI **SUPERCOMPUTER**' (16 characters per line, at the limit; check the render for overflow) would tie it to AI and to slide 2's 'AI data center'. Not required. Other options: option 1 ('AI COMPUTE ISN'T JUST CHATBOTS', myth-flip) names no company and the slides never mention chatbots or say anyone believes compute is only for chatbots, so the myth is invented and the label is weaker; it is also less clear at a glance ('compute' is jargon for ESL readers). Option 2 ('HYUNDAI: $6.7B FOR AN AI HUB', number) is the label-honest but the riskiest: the $6.7B (9 trillion won) is a regional investment commitment (Korea Times) or the whole AI Valley project (ZDNet Korea), not the data center cost, and 'FOR AN AI HUB' on the cover would make the slides break the promise on slide 6. The writer's reasoning for rejecting it is sound. Chosen hook is the best of the three. hook_types labels: claim, myth-flip (shaky but not dishonest about being reader-impact), number are all acceptable; none claims reader-impact. hook_pick_reason contains an honest 'No reader-impact hook:' reason (the articles say nothing about effects on ordinary readers), so that check is satisfied. Slide 2 renders cleanly with no overflow; kicker '02 / 08' and 8 progress dots are consistent.
